Hi Elena — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a first pass MAP that pairs acceptance tests with decision gates and owners. Summary below:

- Acceptance tests: functional correctness (10 representative prompts), throughput (95th pct latency at 512 tokens), safety/concordance checks (50 edge cases), and end-to-end integration smoke (API + prefix cache behavior).
- Exit gates: pass rate >= 95% for correctness, latency SLO met in 3/4 traffic scenarios, no critical security findings in baseline scan.
- Owners & timeline: we propose a 3-week sprint: week 1 = onboarding + baseline runs; week 2 = targeted tuning & retest; week 3 = final verification + stakeholder demo.

Attachments: CuraTech-Redwood-MAP-v3.pdf (draft MAP), acceptance-tests-runbook.xlsx (test matrix + scripts).

Can Camila and Priyom weigh in on the test owners and any contract/ops caveats?

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez

mateo@redwood.ai

From: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: MAP + acceptance criteria for evaluation

Adding detail on the acceptance tests and owners so the MAP is actionable:

- Functional correctness (Owner: Camila) — testset: 10 prioritized scenarios from CuraTech sample corpus; metric: top-1 exactness and semantic-match score >= 0.92; run: local run + hosted run to compare model variants.
- Latency & throughput (Owner: Mateo) — targets: p95 <= 280ms for 128-token runs, <= 620ms for 512 tokens under steady-state traffic (50 rps); instrumentation: token-level breakdown from Redwood Console and synthetic JMeter harness.
- Safety / Risk checks (Owner: Priyom) — run curated adversarial prompts (50 cases) and apply concordance threshold; also include data-retention verification (no request bodies logged beyond 30 days in staging).
- Integration smoke (Owner: Camila & Eng contact at CuraTech) — verify prefix caching behavior across 3 session types and failover to fallback variant.

Proposed pass/fail rule per test: a single critical regression (security finding or >20% failed correctness on a scenario) triggers a stop-and-fix and pauses signoff. Non-critical regressions should map to mitigation tickets with a checkpoint 48 hours after fix deployment.

I've updated acceptance-tests-runbook.xlsx with owner columns and a pass/fail rubric. Also added a one-page demo checklist (demo-checklist.md) for the final stakeholder walkthrough.

Camila Reyes
Product Solutions, Redwood Inference

Team — thank you, this is exactly what procurement and security wanted. A couple of clarifying items before signoff:

1) For the latency targets, procurement asked for a single-line explanation we can attach to the MAP that explains how p95 was measured (steady-state synthetic harness vs. mixed real traffic). Could you provide that in plain language?
2) For the pass/fail rule: we want the exact rollback trigger defined in the MAP (if >1 critical regression across any two tests, the evaluation halts). Can you add that explicit numeric trigger?
3) We will sign the MAP once the IP allowlist and the pilot SLA excerpt are embedded in the same document (procurement wants a single PDF).

If you can send the revised PDF by Monday (Aug 2) we will route it to legal and aim to sign mid-week.

Best,
Elena
